question: Do quantum responses generated from Fibonacci and M9 P24 representations improve our ability to predict transcription factor occupancy around OXTR?
scope: The first measurement phase has completed CPU and GPU checks and all 16 Aquila programs. Held-out occupancy prediction remains to be evaluated.

beta.endpoint_rule: Exclude endpoints, include wraparound; raw residues used for sums. Empty interiors sum to zero.

epsilon.status: Proposed geometric traversal; physical interpretation not assessed.

atlas.grids: Alpha/Gamma/Epsilon: 24 period positions; Beta: 9 residue positions

reference.selection: Ensembl OXTR gene body plus 10,000 bases on each genomic side
reference.scope: A defined locus window; distal regulatory elements outside it are not captured. Overlapping records may extend beyond its boundaries.
reference.direction: OXTR minus strand; descending genomic coordinates

template.geometry: Six sites on a regular hexagon; ring radius and nearest-neighbour separation 9 micrometres, with one vertex at north. Positions are fixed throughout each run.
template.input: A 24-slot vector of motif/spacing descriptors. Each encoding uses the same source features and identical normalization fitted on training data only.
template.encoding: Global detuning varies with the input; fixed nonzero drive permits noncommuting evolution. Canonical representation weights/order define registered alternatives. No local detuning access is assumed.
template.output: Six excitation probabilities and fifteen labelled pair probabilities at the final time; additional times require distinct tasks and a new frozen version.
template.model: H(t)/hbar = Omega(t)/2 sum_i X_i - Delta_x(t) sum_i n_i + sum_i<j C6/r_ij^6 n_i n_j
template.c6_source: Read and freeze Aquila device capabilities at compilation; never infer a molecular interaction from this Hamiltonian.
template.symmetry: Global driving of this symmetric array can produce redundant single-site and pair features. Measure effective feature rank on training data and retain the same symmetry treatment across all encodings; six atoms do not imply 21 independent features.

variants.label: Ordinary representation
variants.role: Same biological descriptors in their original genomic order.

variants.label: Native Fibonacci
variants.role: Predeclared distance features from native Fibonacci gaps, with the physical base-pair range fixed before labels are inspected.

variants.label: Phi Ratio
variants.role: Ratios of neighbouring motif gaps; retain physical gaps and distinguish native ratios from modular residues.

variants.label: Alpha · M9 P24
variants.role: Full canonical residue order; never equate 24 period positions with 24 hours or a universal 24-base spacing.

variants.label: Beta · M9 P24
variants.role: Canonical 4,8,7,5,1,2 cycle. Six-of-nine membership alone is a broad divisibility feature.

variants.label: Gamma · M9 P24
variants.role: Canonical two-triangle order encoded in time. Shared positions alone do not distinguish Epsilon.

variants.label: Epsilon · M9 P24
variants.role: Canonical seven-visit path, with the repeated closing point retained. A timed encoding must pass a distinguishability check.

variants.label: Matched shuffled representations
variants.role: Seeded controls preserve feature distributions, pulse duration, energy-scale bounds and input information.

evaluation.target: Presence of reproducible TF occupancy in a defined assay and cell context; no claim of exact contact bases, affinity or causal regulation.
evaluation.selection_rule: Choose one human GRCh38 TF assay with replicates, appropriate controls, adequate locus coverage and no dependence on Fibonacci fit. Record accession, factor, cell, QC and label rules before fitting.
inputs: Predefined Fibonacci, Phi Ratio and M9 P24 descriptors
not_inputs: Experimental occupancy labels or ChIP signal
Assay-specific labels used to choose encodings
evaluation.splits: Chromosome/block-separated training and validation, with chr3/OXTR withheld from all fitting. Keep overlapping windows and biological replicates together.
evaluation.primary_metric: Difference in average precision on the frozen independent test set, QRC versus the strongest validation-selected classical model on identical inputs.
controls: Classical nonlinear model with identical representation features
CUDA-Q simulated reservoir using the same physical program
Matched shuffled encoding and label-permutation checks
secondary: Calibration and precision at a fixed recall
Sensitivity to window origin, strand and measurement uncertainty
evaluation.success: Positive held-out improvement with a prespecified uncertainty interval; report inconclusive or negative results without selecting a favourable encoding after testing. No speedup or aromatic mechanism follows from classification alone.
evaluation.uncertainty: Bootstrap independent genomic blocks, keep repeat shots within their sample, report intervals. A locus with too few labels receives a ranking with uncertainty, not a predictive-performance claim.

execution.simulation_route: Compile a checked time-evolution circuit, validate locally, then use the existing qBraid GPU route for supported compiled programs. Native CUDA-Q dynamics is an alternative only after runtime capability checks.
execution.parity: Identical coordinates, C6, pulse schedule, basis/readout convention and observation times. Freeze the discretized AHS program before compiling the matched simulation.
execution.budget_rule: No dispatch until the complete task count, provider quotes and shared budget reservation are recorded and approved for the run. Existing one-task approval is not reused.
execution.task_formula: number of frozen input windows × encoding variants × readout times × hardware repeats

cache.rule: Show cache provenance and run date. A replay of saved results never creates a new hardware receipt. A changed input or model invalidates its dependent result.

review.next: Evaluate the prespecified prediction benchmark against held-out biological observations.

delivery.simulation: Approximately 5–10 minutes from processing start, including the classical calculation and CUDA-Q simulation. Planning estimate; queue and workload can extend it.
delivery.hardware: Timing varies with device availability and the quantum queue. The 25 October 2026 qualification batch completed in 16 minutes 51 seconds from first submission to final completion; the earlier two-atom test took 18 hours 52 minutes. Observed timings are not delivery guarantees.
delivery.report: Publish simulation findings first, then the combined report after hardware completion and evaluation. Clearly identify each version.
delivery.notification: Optional email with verified consent at study launch; send a private return link without biological data in the message. Email delivery is not active in this design review.
delivery.persistence: The review interface saves an optional study record and delivery preference on this device. Execution requires a durable study record independent of browser lifetime.
delivery.classical: Approximately 5–10 minutes from processing start, including the classical calculation and CUDA-Q simulation. Planning estimate; queue and workload can extend it.

roadmap.title: Drug Discovery Network & Open Source Genomic Insights
roadmap.sharing: No active external submission or publishing connection. Future automation retains human oversight.

qualification.scope: Execution and numerical qualification; no biological prediction result.
